games.title: Celis
games.author: Grzegorz “GAD” Drozd
games.description: A side-scrolling shooter for MS-DOS written in Turbo Pascal, which its author compares to Gradius, R-Type and Zybex. The repository labels the build “demo version 0.667” and says the game was never finished but is playable. Packaged from the project’s own files at commit 01bea78; the VGA, memory and Sound Blaster settings come from the DOSBox config the author ships in DOSBox/Celis.conf.
games.rights: GPL-3.0. The copyright holder published the game, its data files and its source in this repository under the GPL, so hosting an unmodified build is permission the licence itself grants — no aggregator label, no upload from a third party, no ROM site. The licence text ships inside the bundle as LICENSE.TXT and the source is the repository at the commit below.

games.title: Sadist
games.author: Grzegorz “GAD” Drozd
games.description: A 1998 DOS game by Grzegorz “GAD” Drozd, who published it — binaries, data, artwork and the Turbo Pascal source — under the GPL. Packaged from commit 2372676 with the files the source opens at runtime: GRAF.DAT, SADIST.DAT, both .CFG files, the character packs in POSTACI/, the terrain packs in TERENY/ and the loose bitmaps and WAV banks lifted out of Data/. Its audio is wired to a Sound Blaster 16 in the bundle’s dosbox.conf.
games.rights: GPL-3.0. The copyright holder published the game, its data files and its source in this repository under the GPL, so hosting an unmodified build is permission the licence itself grants — no aggregator label, no upload from a third party, no ROM site. The licence text ships inside the bundle as LICENSE.TXT and the source is the repository at the commit below.

games.title: Out of Cash
games.author: warrior-rockk
games.description: A point-and-click graphic adventure: your favourite rock band is in town, the ticket costs money you do not have, and the plan is deception. Written for DOS with DJGPP and Allegro and released under the GPL. This bundle is the project’s own published web/out-of-cash.jsdos, byte for byte from commit 8dd5c62 — not repacked here, so its own dosbox.conf and CWSDPMI are exactly as its author tested them.
games.rights: GPL-3.0, published by the game’s author with its source. The .jsdos bundle is the project’s own committed build, served unmodified; the licence text sits beside this shelf in public/retro/licenses/ and the source is the repository at the commit below.

games.title: Moth Hunter
games.tagline: A 508-byte arcade game for the mouse
games.author: Krzysztof Krystian Jankowski
games.description: One .COM file, 508 bytes: it switches the machine to VGA mode 13h, sets up a double buffer, hides the cursor and runs a mouse-aimed shooting loop against alien sprites, with health, hits and a game-over state. Part of x86-assembly, the author’s collection of programs written small on purpose for 8086-class machines. Packaged from dos/game7/game7.com at commit 83a8662, with the MIT licence beside it; the .asm source is in the repository.
games.rights: MIT (c) Krzysztof Krystian Jankowski, who published both the .COM build and the assembly source in this repository under that licence. An unmodified copy of the build is packaged here with the MIT text as LICENSE.TXT, which is the notice the licence asks us to keep.

games.title: Super Vinnie-Pooh
games.tagline: A 1995 platformer, open-sourced by its author
games.author: Mikhail Bratus (FaMe SoftWare)
games.description: A platformer from 1995, sold commercially in Russia as Super Vinnie-Pooh and published by its author — code, graphics, levels — under Apache-2.0 in 2022. Packaged from commit b84f07b with POOH.EXE, the ten .FMS sprite banks, the three .FML graphics and level libraries, its config and the original 1995 readme. The game text is Russian; nothing here was translated or redrawn.
games.rights: Apache-2.0, granted by the game’s author and copyright holder, Mikhail Bratus, who added the licence file to this repository in 2022 next to the source and the assets. The build shipped here is his published POOH.exe plus the data files its code opens; no third-party art or sound.

games.title: Floppybird
games.author: Mihail Szabolcs
games.description: A clone of Flappy Bird written in 16-bit x86 assembly. The repository builds two things from one source: a raw-metal boot image for a floppy, and this 8 704-byte .COM that runs under DOS — its own Makefile starts it with dosbox -conf dosbox.conf build/flpybird.com. Packaged from commit 511ffa5 with the MIT text; the .tga graphics it draws are the author’s own files from the same repository.
games.rights: MIT (c) Mihail Szabolcs, who published the source, the .COM build and the sprite data in this repository under that licence. Served unmodified with the MIT text as LICENSE.TXT.

games.title: nasm-tetris
games.tagline: An unofficial Tetris clone in 2 820 bytes
games.author: Arkadiusz Placha
games.description: In the author’s words: an unofficial Tetris clone for DOS, written purely in NASM assembly. The whole game is the single 2 820-byte TETRIS.EXE in bin/, drawn in text mode, with its assembly source beside it in the repository. Packaged from commit 3fc9598 with the MIT licence and the readme. It is a clone — the name belongs to somebody else, and this site does not present it as the original.
games.rights: MIT (c) Arkadiusz Placha: his own clone, his own assembly source, published together under that licence. The MIT text ships inside the bundle as LICENSE.TXT.

games.title: Snake (54 bytes)
games.tagline: A whole game in 54 bytes of machine code
games.author: donno2048
games.description: A complete snake game in 54 bytes of 16-bit x86 machine code — a code-golf exercise that draws in VGA mode 13h, reads the arrow keys straight from the keyboard controller at port 60h and stops on Escape (the pause key pauses). Packaged from commit 45b2117 with the MIT licence; the assembly it is built from, snake.asm, is in the same repository.
games.rights: MIT, published with the .COM and with the assembly source it is generated from, by its author. Fifty-four bytes of machine code; there is no third-party data inside it.

games.title: Wolfenstein 3D
games.tagline: Episode one, the one that started it all
games.author: id Software, published by Apogee
games.description: Castle Wolfenstein, in first person, in 1992, and the reason a generation of PCs got a sound card. This is v1.4 shareware: episode one, Escape from Wolfenstein, with the guard chatter, the dogs and the blue stone walls. Push forward with the up arrow, Ctrl fires, Space opens doors and Esc brings up the menu; the whole file set is the publisher’s distribution copy, unmodified, and still 1.7 MB.
games.rights: id Software’s 1992 shareware episode, distributed by Apogee, who encouraged readers to copy and pass it on without charge. Shareware edition only — episodes two to six were sold. Files unmodified, no charge, archive pinned by digest. Wolfenstein is a trademark of id Software; this site is not affiliated.

games.title: Commander Keen 4
games.author: id Software, published by Apogee
games.description: Secret of the Oracle: eight-year-old Billy Blaze lands on Gnosticus IV, meets the Oracle and sets off to rescue the Council Members. id’s smooth-scrolling EGA platformer is 805 KB of cartridges and dopefish, and this is the shareware episode in full, not a demo. Arrows walk, Ctrl jumps, Enter uses a door, and the VENDOR.DOC that permits copying is inside the cartridge along with the game.
games.rights: id Software’s shareware episode, licensed for distribution by Apogee, whose VENDOR.DOC in this bundle says everyone "can -- and is encouraged! -- to copy, upload and generally pass around this Program without charging for it". Unmodified, no charge. Commander Keen is a trademark of id Software; this site is not affiliated.

games.title: Jazz Jackrabbit
games.author: Epic MegaGames
games.description: A 256-colour VGA platformer with a soundtrack by Robert A. Allen and Alexander Brandon, running at a speed that made 1994 hardware look slow. This is the shareware episode, Turtle Terror, with its own menu, its own demos and 84 files of MOD music and sprite banks, exactly as Epic packaged it. Arrows run and jump up, Ctrl fires, Enter confirms. Epic’s LICENSE.DOC, which permits the copying, ships inside the cartridge.
games.rights: Epic MegaGames shareware episode one of six. Epic’s LICENSE.DOC in this bundle permits and encourages redistribution by BBS and online service provided no files are altered or removed, which is why the release ships complete and unmodified, at no charge. Jazz Jackrabbit is a trademark of Epic Games; this site is not affiliated.

games.title: Duke Nukem 3D
games.author: 3D Realms
games.description: The Build engine, a strip club, a shrink ray and a Duke who will not shut up: the 1996 shareware release, v1.3D, all 12.9 MB of DUKE3D.GRP included. This is episode one, L.A. Meltdown, the one everybody actually played. Arrows move and turn, Ctrl fires, Space jumps, and the in-game help is on F1. 3D Realms’ LICENSE.DOC is in the cartridge and asks only that copies be given away free.
games.rights: 3D Realms’ 1996 shareware release, episode one of four. Its LICENSE.DOC, shipped here, grants "LIMITED DISTRIBUTION RIGHTS": individuals "can -- and are encouraged! -- to give away copies of the Game without charge". Registered episodes are not present. Duke Nukem is a trademark of Gearbox; this site is not affiliated.

games.title: Heretic
games.tagline: City of the Damned, shareware episode
games.author: Raven Software, published by id Software
games.description: Raven took the DOOM engine, replaced the space station with a cathedral and gave the player a crossbow that freezes people. This is the shareware episode, City of the Damned, with HERETIC1.WAD and the release’s own LICENSE.DOC. It launches straight into the first level because id’s engine understands -warp; arrows move, Ctrl fires, Space opens doors, and F1 shows the keys.
games.rights: id Software’s shareware release of Heretic, licensed by its own LICENSE.DOC, which covers "the shareware version or episode one" and is shipped unmodified in this bundle. VENDOR.DOC routes retail resale through GT Interactive and exempts BBS and FTP distribution. No charge for this copy; registered episodes absent.

games.title: Rise of the Triad
games.author: Apogee Software
games.description: The loudest game Apogee ever shipped: monks, missile launchers, a score counter lifted from pinball and an episode that ends with you flying a hang glider. ROTT’s shareware build is episode one, and its VENDOR.DOC is emphatic about what that means — "No right is given by this Vendor.Doc to copy, use or distribute any other version". Arrows move, Ctrl fires, Space jumps, Enter confirms.
games.rights: Apogee’s shareware release, marked "Shareware" and containing "episode #1" as its VENDOR.DOC requires; that document also states everyone is encouraged to pass it around without charge. Unmodified, complete, no fee. Registered episodes are not here. Rise of the Triad is a trademark of its owners; this site is not affiliated.

games.title: Blake Stone
games.author: Jam Productions, published by Apogee
games.description: A British agent, a lunar base and the last game Apogee shipped on the Wolfenstein engine — with ceilings and floors, animated walls and an informant who sells you hints for credits. The shareware release runs the first floors of Aliens of Gold. Arrows move, Ctrl fires, Space opens doors, and the VENDOR.DOC granting the copying is inside the cartridge rather than paraphrased on a card.
games.rights: Jam Productions’ shareware release, licensed for distribution by Apogee: its VENDOR.DOC, shipped unmodified in this bundle, encourages everyone to "copy, upload and generally pass around this Program without charging for it". No charge, no registered content. Blake Stone is a trademark of its owners; this site is not affiliated.

games.title: Raptor
games.tagline: Call of the Shadows, shareware release
games.author: Cygnus Studios, published by Apogee
games.description: The vertical shooter that sold a million shareware copies: a mercenary pilot buying better guns between waves of tanks, gunboats and things with too many engines. Apogee shipped it on three disks with a shop, a soundtrack and 5 MB of artwork, all of which is here. Arrows fly, Ctrl fires, Alt fires a missile, Enter confirms a menu entry.
games.rights: Cygnus Studios’ shareware release, distributed by Apogee. Its VENDOR.DOC in this bundle reads: everyone "can -- and is encouraged! -- to copy, upload and generally pass around this Program without charging for it". Shipped complete and unmodified, at no charge. Raptor is a trademark of its owners; this site is not affiliated.

games.title: Hocus Pocus
games.author: Moonlite Software, published by Apogee
games.description: A wizard’s apprentice collects crystals across 320×200 VGA levels while a soundtrack by the Fat Man plays behind him. Moonlite’s game was the first Apogee platformer with a scrolling background and a shop, and the shareware release is the opening levels in full. Arrows walk, Ctrl jumps, Space casts, Enter picks a menu entry.
games.rights: Moonlite Software’s shareware release, distributed by Apogee, whose VENDOR.DOC ships in this bundle and encourages everyone to copy and pass the program around without charge. Files unmodified, no charge, no registered levels. Hocus Pocus is a trademark of its owners; this site is not affiliated.

games.title: Jill of the Jungle
games.author: Epic MegaGames
games.description: Tim Sweeney wrote the engine, Allen Pilgrim drew the jungle, and Jill jumped through it in 16 colours with a knife and a key. Episode one is 1.1 MB and loads instantly, which is how a whole generation met Epic before Jazz and Unreal. Arrows move, Ctrl jumps, Space uses a weapon, and Epic’s LICENSE.DOC — the permission to copy — is inside the cartridge.
games.rights: Epic MegaGames shareware episode one. Epic’s LICENSE.DOC in this bundle says readers are "permitted, and encouraged, to make and distribute copies of the Program to their friends, family members and co-workers without charge". Unmodified, no fee, no registered episodes. Jill of the Jungle is a trademark of Epic Games.

games.title: DOOM
games.author: id Software
games.description: Episode one, Knee-Deep in the Dead, exactly as id shipped it in 1994: DOOM.EXE v1.9 and DOOM1.WAD, byte for byte, with the README that came in the archive. The IWAD is checked against the SHA-256 of the official 4,196,020-byte shareware file every time the bundle is built, so what runs here is id’s own release and not a repack. Arrow keys move and turn, Ctrl fires, Space opens doors, F1 shows the key card.
games.rights: id Software’s shareware release. John Carmack, 23 Oct 1999: "The DOOM shareware wad is freely distributable." Debian ships these files as doom-wad-shareware on that basis; RPM Fusion as doom-shareware, License: Distributable. Unmodified, no charge, registered episodes excluded. DOOM is a trademark of id Software; this site is not affiliated.
